*Part X · Reference*

# 28. Sources

*The book's own sources are Trustwork's record: its decision records, handbook chapters, status page and launch playbooks. Those need no link here and are named without repository paths. Below are the outside facts the book relies on, grouped by theme, each with its publisher, title, year and link, read on 4 November 2026 unless another date is given, with its evidence level where it matters; and, at the end, what the sources leave open. A plain entry is a primary or official source; "secondary" marks press, encyclopaedias, law-firm notes and aggregators; "self claim" marks what an organisation says about itself. The Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 and the FATF lists were read only from secondary summaries and appear in the book as reported.*

## Trustwork's own documents

- Trustwork's vision, status ("What works today, and what is designed"), roadmap, hubs, federation and federation protocol, the hub operating company, your agent, execution and reputation, learning, events, the magazine, the tender desk, procurement and supply, discovery and outreach, country specifics, localization, brand and open-source governance, in its public repository under Contribuda, snapshot of 4 November 2026.
- Trustwork's decision records 009 to 028, including ADR 010 (the gathering point, hubs, agents and the mesh), ADR 014 (the sanctions compliance engine), ADR 018 (the hub operating company), ADR 027 (sealed requests for quotes) and ADR 028 (the open and free engine, income kept in each country, Contribuda's international part and the reference hub), each dated.
- Trustwork's launch playbook and the ten country playbooks (Peru, the Philippines, Kenya, Ghana, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Uzbekistan, Nigeria, Mexico, Rwanda), and the top-ten launch-country research of November 2026 (sources accessed 31 October 2026), all Proposed.

## Open source, public bodies and public tenders

For chapter 7. The principle that the engine is open and free is Trustwork's own decision of November 2026; the facts below support the argument. No quantified saving from open source in public procurement was found in a primary source, and none is quoted.

- Interoperable Europe Act: Regulation (EU) 2024/903, in force 11 April 2024; prioritise solutions without restrictive licensing terms where equivalent in functionalities, total cost and cybersecurity; share solutions incl. source code (2024; official summary and secondary): [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/interoperable-europe-act.html), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interoperable_Europe_Act), [datos.gob.es](https://datos.gob.es/en/blog/interoperable-europe-act).
- European Commission, guidelines on sharing interoperability solutions: [pathway 1](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/guidelines-sharing-interoperability-solutions/pathway-1) (Article 4(6): prioritise solutions without restrictive licensing terms where equivalent in functionalities, total cost, user-centricity, cybersecurity or other relevant objective criteria) and [pathway 3](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/guidelines-sharing-interoperability-solutions/pathway-3) (Article 4(1): sharing, on request, of interoperability solutions behind trans-European digital public services, with documentation and, where available, source code) (2024; primary).
- Commission open source strategy 2020–2023 ("think open") (2020; primary): [European Commission](https://commission.europa.eu/departments/informatics/open-source-software-strategy_en).
- Commission study: lower TCO, less vendor lock-in, more digital autonomy; no saving figure quoted (2021; primary (press release)): [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-publishes-study-impact-open-source-european-economy).
- "If it is public money, it should be public code as well"; over 200 organisations and more than 31,000 individuals (2017–; self claim (figures); secondary): [FSFE](https://fsfe.org/activities/publiccode/publiccode.en.html), [LWN](https://lwn.net/Articles/734169/).
- India 2015 policy: OSS preferred; strategic control and lifetime cost among criteria (2015; secondary; primary): [SFLC.in](https://sflc.in/policies-and-cases/policy-on-adoption-of-open-source-software-for-government-of-india/), [DeitY](https://egovstandards.gov.in/sites/default/files/2021-07/Framework%20for%20Adoption%20of%20Open%20Source%20Software%20in%20e-Governance%20Systems.pdf).
- France 2016 law: source code a communicable administrative document (2016; secondary): [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loi_pour_une_République_numérique), [CMS](https://cms.law/en/fra/legal-updates/logiciel-libre-objectif-d-ouverture-des-codes-sources).
- Brazil: free software public policy since 2003; public software portal 2007 (c. 2011–2013; primary (dated); secondary): [Serpro](https://www.serpro.gov.br/menu/noticias/noticias-antigas/governo-aprimora-modelo-do-software-publico), [ENAP](https://repositorio.enap.gov.br/handle/1/349).
- Germany: ZenDiS founded December 2022; openDesk (2022–2025; vendor/self; secondary): [ZenDiS](https://opendesk.eu/en/about), [Commission OSOR](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/open-source-observatory-osor/news/bwibundeswehr-chooses-open-source-adopting-opendesk).
- Schleswig-Holstein: April 2024 decision, about 30,000 workstations to LibreOffice; sovereignty (2024; secondary): [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2024/04/04/germanys_northernmost_state_ditches_windows/).
- Denmark's digital ministry leaving Microsoft Office, June 2025 (2025; secondary): [Computing](https://www.computing.co.uk/news/2025/denmark-digital-ministry-drops-microsoft), [heise](https://heise.de/-10438942).
- Lyon leaving Microsoft, June 2025 (2025; secondary): [Commission OSOR](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/open-source-observatory-osor/news/municipality-lyon-moves-towards-open-source), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2025/06/26/lyon_leaving_microsoft/).
- UN SG Roadmap for Digital Cooperation, 11 June 2020: concerted global effort to invest in digital public goods (2020; primary): [United Nations](https://www.un.org/en/content/digital-cooperation-roadmap).
- Global Digital Compact, 22 Sept 2024: invest in DPGs and DPI by 2030 (2024; primary): [United Nations](https://www.un.org/global-digital-compact).
- DPG Standard: nine indicators, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (2026; primary): [DPGA](https://www.digitalpublicgoods.net/standard).
- GovStack led by BMZ/GIZ, Estonia, ITU, DIAL; openness and reusability (2026; primary/self): [GovStack](https://www.govstack.global/about/).
- Decidim: more than 450 organisations; 574 instances, 36 countries (self); AGPL; DPG (2025–2026; self claim; primary): [Decidim](http://decidim.org/usedby), [DPGA](https://www.digitalpublicgoods.net/r/decidim), [FOSDEM](https://fosdem.org/2025/events/attachments/fosdem-2025-5458-how-a-city-platform-became-a-global-community/slides/236928/Decidim_F_SHW2cZd.pdf).
- Decidim 2022: two workers paid from two €50,000 grants; diversification (2025; primary/self): [Decidim at FOSDEM](https://fosdem.org/schedule/event/fosdem-2025-5552-building-sustainability-a-case-study-in-funding-diversification-for-decidim).
- Consul Democracy: more than 250 cities and organisations (self); Foundation 2019, no developers, struggles financially; Munich €20,000 a year; Scotland COSLA 32 councils (2025–2026; self claim; secondary): [Consul Democracy](https://consuldemocracy.org/), [Commission OSOR](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/open-source-observatory-osor/document/case-study-consul-democracy).
- X-Road core MIT-licensed since 3 Oct 2016; NIIS founded 2017 by Estonia and Finland; Iceland's Straumurinn from Nov 2018 (2016–2021; secondary; primary; self): [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Road), [Digital Iceland](https://island.is/en/o/digital-iceland/straumurinn-x-road), [NIIS](https://niis.org/blog/2018/5/27/changes-in-the-x-road-development).

## Financing private construction

- How a private build is financed where it is: Fannie Mae Selling Guide, [B5-3.1-02, single-closing construction-to-permanent](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b5-3.1-02/conversion-construction-permanent-financing-single-closing-transactions) and its [lender job aid](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/media/6311/display) on draws, holdbacks and lien waivers (secondary); MISMO, [about](https://www.mismo.org/about-mismo) (self claim on benefits); US Census, [construction spending](https://www.census.gov/construction/c30/c30index.html); BuildStore, [how self-build mortgages work](https://www.buildstore.co.uk/mortgages-finance/project-types/self-build-mortgages/how-self-build-mortgages-work) (vendor); NHBC, [Buildmark cover](https://www.nhbc.co.uk/homeowners/what-does-buildmark-cover); [NaCSBA](https://nacsba.org.uk/); Germany's [§ 3 MaBV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewo_34cdv/__3.html) and Dr. Klein, [Baufortschritt](https://www.drklein.de/baufortschritt-auszahlung-baukredit.html), 2024 (secondary); France's décennale and dommages-ouvrage on service-public.gouv.fr (sheets F2034 and F2032); RICS, [valuation of development property](https://www.rics.org/profession-standards/rics-standards-and-guidance/sector-standards/valuation-standards/valuation-of-development-property); IRMI, [builder's risk](https://www.irmi.com/term/insurance-definitions/builders-risk-policy) and [surety](https://surety.org/what-is-surety/) (secondary definitions).
- The launch countries: Peru's Techo Propio via [Andina](https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-techo-propio-ministerio-vivienda-entregara-6698-bonos-vivienda-12-regiones-1039925.aspx), 2025 (state agency citing a ministerial resolution), [La Cámara](https://www.lacamara.pe/bono-techo-propio-2025-asi-puedes-acceder-al-subsidio-de-s-32-100-para-construir-tu-casa/) (secondary) and [Fondo Mivivienda](https://fondomivivienda.pe/); [Mibanco](https://www.mibanco.com.pe/prestamos/construccion-vivienda) (vendor); Mexico's ConstruYO via [El Imparcial](https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2025/02/06/construir-una-casa-con-infonavit-en-tu-terreno-te-presta-lo-mismo-que-al-comprar), 2025 (secondary) and CONAVI headlines; the Philippines' Pag-IBIG tranches via [Respicio & Co.](https://www.respicio.ph/commentaries/how-to-resolve-a-delayed-pag-ibig-loan-release), 2026 (secondary); Kenya: [KMRC](https://kmrc.co.ke/), [Business Daily, 2022](https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/markets/capital-markets/banks-make-4-5pc-margin-on-cheaper-mortgages-scheme-3875392) and [2018](https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/corporate/companies/study-tips-micro-loans-to-bridge-housing-shortfall-among-poor-2198000) (secondary), the World Bank's Kenya Affordable Housing Finance Project (P165034) and Rwanda Housing Finance Project (P165649) from the projects API; Nigeria: [Family Homes Funds](https://fhfl.com.ng/) (self claim), NMRC (secondary); Colombia: Fonvivienda, [Resolución 0813 de 2025](https://www.minvivienda.gov.co/sites/default/files/normativa/0813-2025.pdf), and El Cronista Colombia on the November 2025 decree (secondary); Uzbekistan: ADB, [Expanding access to housing in Uzbekistan through market reforms](https://development.asia/case-study/expanding-access-housing-uzbekistan-through-market-reforms).

- Precedents used in chapters 10, 20 and 21: Nepal's homeowner-driven reconstruction, Morocco's supervised self-construction and Sindh's owner-driven housing (above); CEMEX's Patrimonio Hoy (vendor figures, above); the Durban community construction management teams in the World Cities Report 2026 (above).
- Payment rails named in chapter 21 are the publicly operated national systems and licensed providers of each country, named for their public existence. The Dominican instant-payment system planned by the Banco Central for 2027: Revista Mercado, [the central bank's payment infrastructure from 2027](https://revistamercado.do/money-invest/daily-news/nueva-infraestructura-de-pagos-busca-acelerar-la-economia-digital-dominicana-asi-funcionara-el-sistema-del-banco-central-desde-2027/), 2025 (secondary).

## A home that remembers

- The home as the largest asset: OECD, [Housing Taxation in OECD Countries: Highlights](https://www.oecd.org/tax/tax-policy/brochure-housing-taxation-in-oecd-countries.pdf), 2022; OECD, [Inheritance Taxation in OECD Countries](https://www.oecd.org/tax/tax-policy/inheritance-taxation-in-oecd-countries-presentation-may-2021.pdf), presentation, May 2021; European Central Bank, [Household Finance and Consumption Survey: Results from the 2021 wave](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/scpsps/ecb.sps46~3563bc9f03.en.pdf), Statistics Paper 46, 2023; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, [Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2019 to 2022](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/files/scf23.pdf), October 2023; HM Revenue and Customs, [Inheritance tax liabilities statistics: commentary](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/inheritance-tax-liabilities-statistics/inheritance-tax-liabilities-statistics-commentary), 2023 to 2024; World Bank, [land and housing as the assets of the poor](https://ppp.worldbank.org/node/9456); Andina, reporting the Ministerio de Vivienda, [about seventy per cent of Peru's homes are self-built](https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-ministerio-vivienda-alista-propuesta-para-reducir-riesgos-viviendas-autoconstruidas-850718.aspx), 25 June 2021 (official statement via the state news agency).
- A house that remembers: Housing History Information Accumulation and Utilisation Promotion Council, [presentation to MLIT's committee on long-life quality housing](https://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001271071.pdf), 29 January 2019 (3.57 million dwellings; the common house ID; the council's purpose); MLIT, [long-life quality housing certifications, FY2024](https://www.mlit.go.jp/report/press/house04_hh_001283.html), 27 June 2025; Organization for Housing Warranty, [Housing Warranty Scheme in Japan](https://www.how.or.jp/information/docs/Housing%20Warranty%20Scheme%20in%20Japan%20Dec2022.pdf), December 2022 (industry body; the 2000 and 2009 laws, the water-ingress share, the quoted account of the 2005 fraud); Interoperable Europe, [Building passport Flanders: Woningpas](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/egovernment/solution/building-passport-flanders-woningpas) (self-description by the public operator) and Vlaams Energie- en Klimaatagentschap, [Woningpas en gebouwenpas in 2025](https://www.vlaanderen.be/veka/woningpas-en-gebouwenpas-zorgen-voor-digitale-sprong-vooruit-in-2025); Légifrance, [Loi n° 2021-1104, article 167](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/article_jo/JORFARTI000043957107) (the carnet d'information du logement); European Commission, [study on an EU framework for digital building logbooks](https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/growth/items/690184), 2020; Gokarakonda and Toth, [A framework for digital building logbooks](https://www.bpie.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/A-framework-for-digital-building-logbooks-Drivers-of-affordable-circular-and-sustainable-built-environment.pdf), eceee Summer Study, 2026 (secondary; the source for the 2024 directive's definition); UK Government, [HIPs failed because no one trusted them](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/hips-failed-because-no-one-trusted-them), 10 September 2010, and the [impact assessment](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/abolishing-home-information-packs-impact-assessment).
- Learning from many homes: Agence Qualité Construction, [Observatoire de la Qualité de la Construction 2025](https://qualiteconstruction.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Rapport-Observatoire-Qualite-Construction-2025-AQC.pdf) and [Sycodés](https://sycodes.qualiteconstruction.com); Byggeskadefonden, [presentation to BL](https://bl.dk/media/l1upwiok/bsf-bl-erfa-moeder-oktober-2024-rev-7102024-241024.pdf), October 2024 (self claim: the fall in serious failures); Sekretariatet for Byggeskadeforsikring, [Årsberetning 2024](https://www.sbst.dk/Media/638790079894689045/rsberetning_2024.pdf) (the self-build exemption); NHBC, [submission to the APPG inquiry](https://www.cic.org.uk/uploads/files/old/nhbc.pdf), 2015 (self claim; read for the chapter, not quoted); Fire and Disaster Management Agency, [deaths in the Kobe earthquake](https://www.fdma.go.jp/relocation/bousai_manual/e/pre/preparation101.html); Alabama Department of Insurance, [FORTIFIED study after Hurricane Sally](https://www.aldoi.gov/currentnewsitem.aspx?ID=1321), 19 May 2025; WBHM, [Strengthen Alabama Homes](https://wbhm.org/2023/an-alabama-program-helps-residents-stormproof-their-homes-louisiana-wants-to-copy-it), 2023 (secondary: the mandatory discount and the grants).
- Free learning and protection: REACH, [Typhoon Haiyan Shelter Response Outcome Assessment](https://repository.impact-initiatives.org/document/reach/9824b43b/phl_report_shelter_recovery_outcome_assessment_may_2016.pdf), May 2016; FEMA, [Homeowner's Guide to Retrofitting](https://www.fema.gov/homeowners-guide-retrofitting); Australian Government, [Your Home](https://www.yourhome.gov.au); UNAM on Coursera, [Cómo autoconstruir tu vivienda](https://www.coursera.org/learn/como-autoconstruir-tu-vivienda) (platform page; enrolment as of November 2026); National Construction Authority (Kenya), [Regulations 2014](https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/2014/74/eng@2022-12-31) (the exemption of skilled workers and site supervisors from registration as contractors) and [accreditation of skilled workers and site supervisors](https://www.nca.go.ke/full-accreditation); Arizona Revised Statutes §32-1132 and 2025 press reports on the Residential Contractors' Recovery Fund (secondary); Bauherren-Schutzbund and Institut für Bauforschung, defects per new house 2020 to 2024, as reported by [Baulinks](https://www.baulinks.de/webplugin/2025/1497.php4), October 2025 (secondary; read for the chapter, not quoted).

## A hub with Contribuda

- Contribuda's public site, contribuddha.com, for what it offers; its internal records are not public and are not cited.
- Trustwork's hub operating company (ADR 018, accepted 1 November 2026; function accountability and the staff lifecycle are Live in the API, the rest open), launch playbook, hubs chapter (the reference hub, launch checklist, second-person activation), hub network and directory design (Proposed), hub console and setup wizard, ADR 012 of 31 October 2026 (decision 26 on the operator of the reference hub), the hub exchange layer (ADR 016 decision 10: each hub charges only its own participant), the licence decision of 29 October 2026 and the open-source governance module, all in its public repository under Contribuda, snapshot of 4 November 2026.

## Organisations named

- Every public body, association, university, training body, newsroom, funder, platform, payment provider and company named in chapters 20 to 22 is named from its own public pages, a public register or the country playbooks, for its public work; naming implies no contact, interest or agreement. Where the book says "connected", and today it says so nowhere for Trustwork, a real integration exists; "planned" means a work package exists.

## What the sources leave open

- For chapter 7: the consolidated text of the Interoperable Europe Act and India's 2015 policy document were read through summaries; whether Schleswig-Holstein's move is complete; the current state of Brazil's public software portal; the exact adoption counts of Consul Democracy and Decidim, which are self-reported and counted differently; and whether public tenders generally score the implementation budget, which the book states as experience and not as a measured finding.
- The Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 scores (read from a secondary table) and the FATF lists of June and October 2026 (read from compliance-firm and regulator summaries); both appear as reported.
- Why the Open Budget Survey 2025 covers 82 countries rather than 125, and whether the countries absent from it will be reported later; any survey result for Uzbekistan.
- Uzbekistan's Open Budget programme: the share of district budgets, the identity-verification design after the 2024 "one citizen, one vote" announcement, and whether the coerced projects of 2025 were finally removed; the vote and winner totals rest on press reports of ministry figures.
- The statute that fixes the share of national transfers Dominican municipalities must spend on capital works (sources attribute it to different laws, so the book names none), Colombia's Law 1757 of 2015 and Law 850 of 2003, Ecuador's territorial code, Kenya's Article 203(2) and Ghana's Article 252, all cited from secondary sources; municipal compliance with the Dominican law (the eight per cent figure is an undated critic's estimate).
- Medellín's share of the investment budget for participatory budgeting and its recent turnout; Mexico City's schedule from three to four per cent and the consolidated share of unexecuted winners.
- The Philippines' Citizen Participatory Audit beyond the survey's scoring, the Bottom-up Budgeting history beyond press, the independent commission's final total of hearings and its final report, and whether the procurement portal now publishes open contracting data.
- Georgia's 2025 foreign-agent and grant laws in detail, its municipal budgets' current state and the 2021 Batumi collapse figures; Armenia's community count after consolidation; Azerbaijan's municipal finance and reconstruction budgets; Rwanda's Kigali informal housing share and the EU measures of March 2025.
- San Diego's 2025 and 2026 homelessness counts by city, the regional housing need figures, and a claimed March 2026 permitting package (unofficial source only); any city-run participatory budget in San Diego (none found).
- DREAM's project counts and Kyiv's public budget status in 2024 to 2026; Honduras' disclosure system status; Mongolia's Glass Account Law details; Senegal's and Kyrgyzstan's current programmes; Tanzania's and Türkiye's partnership status; Prozorro's and DoZorro's 2024 and 2025 totals; Peru's year-end 2025 stalled-works figure of 67 billion soles (single press source).
- CoST's membership status per sub-national entity beyond its own lists; Portal da Transparência's access counts; the current total of the Digital Public Goods registry.
- The "220 million construction workers" figure (not found in a primary ILO source; not used); any independent evaluation of Build Change or Patrimonio Hoy outcomes; Habitat for Humanity's nine-country figures; the exact per-institution trust figures in the OECD reports; Bürokratt's agency count; Singapore's Pair usage (two official figures); the UK's productivity estimate (not audited); whether the FTC's 2024 rule has since been challenged; the reported court ruling on USAID's dismantling.
- Hewlett's and Luminate's 2025 and 2026 grants; the IDB's and AfDB's digital public infrastructure programmes; X-Road's and DHIS2's governance; Decidim's Social Contract wording; the EU Global Gateway figures.
- Financing: the owner-built share of United States starts and specific lenders' owner-builder rules; the UK lenders' handbook wording and Help to Build figures; a primary Bausparkasse source; Pag-IBIG's official checklist content; Infonavit's official ConstruYO page and CONAVI's self-production rules; Mibanco's terms and Techo Propio's minimum saving (two figures in sources); the CAHF Ghana and Rwanda 2024 profiles and the Rwanda project's results; KMRC's current caps and 2025 totals; NMRC's underwriting standards; any micro-insurance for low-income homes in the Philippines or Kenya; partial credit guarantees for self-build; materials companies' credit programmes other than Patrimonio Hoy; no insurer in any launch country could be named from a verified source.
- Current prices of any provider; the book quotes none. The present state of each country's data-protection, outreach, defamation and whistle-blower rules; every such row is for counsel.
- Sources disagree on how many Mexican sub-national bodies publish open contracting data (17 publishers in the registry; "two dozen" state transparency institutes in another reading); the book uses the registry figure. Moldova's open contracting feed and Chișinău's civic budget; the Inter-American Development Bank's housing programmes; and the trade-press count of master builders in a Peruvian cement maker's online community (quoted as reported).
- The comparison sets differ: the civic scorecard uses the fourteen countries of this book; the open-budget comparison uses the fourteen and Ukraine.
- For the chapter on a home that remembers: the main residence's share of total household assets in the ECB's 2021 survey (only ownership rates and median values were read); the OECD inheritance report's share of bequests that are housing; any quantified effect of a house history or maintenance record on resale price, insurability or credit, in Japan or anywhere (the "five to ten per cent premium" circulating online is unsourced and is not used); the exact wording of the digital building logbook definition in Directive (EU) 2024/1275 (the wording rests on a 2026 article); Woningpas user counts (the three million dwellings is the operator's own 2019 figure); independent evaluation of Byggeskadefonden's fall in serious failures (the fund's own figures); Alabama's exact discount percentage and the University of Alabama report itself; whether the UNAM course can be taken free of charge (the certificate is paid); Arizona's recovery fund figures (press only); the Bauherren-Schutzbund defect count (a secondary report of an association's study).
- Ukraine's procurement figures show competitive procurement rising from 616.8 to 841 billion hryvnia between 2023 and 2024; one summary called that a doubling, which the figures do not support, and the book does not say so.
